claims.text: Almost 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower.
Nepal earns nearly $200m (£147m) each year exporting hydroelectricity to India and Bangladesh.
Floods in Nepal severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin and knocked out more than 10% of Nepal's total power generation capacity.
The state-owned Nepal Electricity Authority owns six of the 12 hydropower facilities damaged in the recent floods.
In 2010, only two-thirds of people in Nepal had access to electricity.
Nepal currently has 225 hydropower plants with more than 3,900MW of installed capacity, according to the Nepal Electricity Authority.
High-altitude regions of the Himalayas are warming 50% faster than the global average.
Preliminary investigations indicate a collapsed glacier and its bedrock triggered the recent flash flood in Nepal.
According to Nepal's Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, more than nine in 10 recorded disaster events between 2018 and 2024 were related to climate.
The Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project was valued at about $647m before being nearly destroyed by floods.
Rescuers pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal.
India's Ministry of External Affairs reported that 275 Indian nationals remain missing following flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border.
A total of 166 Indian nationals were rescued after flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border.
The Indian government stated that 1,907 Indian nationals safely crossed into Nepal from China.
India supplied approximately 95 tonnes of relief material on seven aircraft to Nepal following the August 26 flash floods.
India deployed 54 personnel to Nepal, including 30 tunnel rescue experts, 19 forensic experts, and a five-member medical team.
Nepalese authorities reported at least 1,295 people were killed in the floods.
More than 12,000 people have been rescued in Nepal while almost 5,000 remain missing.
Local authorities reported that floods damaged 35 motorable bridges, 45 suspension bridges, and 40 km of black-topped roads in central Nepal.
Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority stated the flash floods were triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border.
The Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority designated Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital in Bengaluru as the nodal centre for collecting DNA samples from relatives of missing persons in Nepal.
A massive landslide occurred at Bhattar in Api Himal Rural Municipality, partially blocking the Chaulani River in Nepal's Darchula district.
The Chaulani River originates in the Api Himal region and joins the Mahakali River along the Nepal-India border.
An eight-year-old A320neo aircraft (VT-EXO) carrying 145 people experienced a near-simultaneous loss of all three hydraulic systems at 36,000 feet.
The flight control system detected the loss of all three hydraulic systems within four seconds at 9:32:43am IST.
During the altitude upset, the aircraft gained 372 feet and dropped by 292 feet from its assigned 36,000 feet level.
The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau expects to publish its final investigation report on or before August 4, 2027.
Air India dismissed the pilot-in-command of its Phuket-Delhi flight after he tested positive for a psychoactive substance.
Both pilots underwent post-flight medical checks in Delhi, where breath analyser tests for alcohol returned satisfactory results.
A confirmatory blood test showed a non-negative result for a psychoactive substance for the pilot-in-command, while the co-pilot tested negative.
Under Directorate General of Civil Aviation rules, a pilot who tests positive for psychoactive substances must undergo rehabilitation before returning to flying duties.
At least 24 people received medical assistance following the flight incident, with at least four suffering serious injuries.
Air India stated that safety remains its highest priority following the termination of the pilot-in-command.
The pilot-in-command was serving as the pilot monitoring and was not handling primary controls during the altitude upset.
The aircraft's flight-control system detected the loss of the green hydraulic system at 09:32 am, followed four seconds later by the loss of the blue and yellow systems.
The blue hydraulic system was restored around 09:32am, followed shortly by the yellow and green systems.
The Airbus A320neo was carrying 137 passengers during the August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight.
The aircraft landed safely at Delhi airport at 11:00 am IST and taxied under its own power to the parking bay.
Technical experts from Airbus inspected the aircraft between August 13 and August 15.
Dalit activist Nishu Aazad's father was injured in an attack during protests at Jantar Mantar.
Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) filed a police complaint against Swatantra Bhardwaj for falsely claiming an association with Union minister Chirag Paswan.
Swatantra Bhardwaj was taken into custody by police in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh.
Chirag Paswan stated he takes full responsibility for pursuing the matter with Delhi Police to ensure justice for Nishu Aazad's father.
In a podcast, Swatantra Bhardwaj claimed he cracked the skull of Sanjay Azad, stating the injury required 60 stitches.
Swatantra Bhardwaj asserted in a podcast that he acted in self-defence after being surrounded by 10 to 15 people.
Nishu Azad is a student activist associated with the Cockroach Janata Party who gained public attention during protests at Jantar Mantar.
Nishu Azad protested outside Parliament Street Police Station alongside political leaders including Chandra Shekhar Aazad.
Sanjay Kumar, father of student activist Nishu Aazad, was assaulted on July 23 at Jantar Mantar during youth protests against exam irregularities.
In a viral video, Swatantra Bhardwaj claimed a phone call from Delhi minister Kapil Mishra helped him avoid arrest.
Cockroach Janta Party members staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station demanding attempt-to-murder charges be added to the FIR.
Swatantra Bhardwaj made anti-Muslim statements during a September 1 podcast interview on 'The Casual Talk' channel.
Swatantra Bhardwaj stated he wants to form a hardline Hindu party focused on creating a Muslim-free India.
Swatantra Bhardwaj threatened to shoot anyone who applied the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against him.
Swatantra Bhardwaj was booked under the POCSO Act on September 4 following allegations of death and rape threats made against a minor activist.
